chunks: Say: 'No one in the heavens and the earth has knowledge of the unknown except God, nor can they know when they will be raised again.'

key_terms.الْغَيْبَ: The unseen or hidden realities known only to God

ai.seo_question: Who has knowledge of the unseen (al-ghayb) according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to refute the claims of prophets and imams possessing independent knowledge of the unseen, affirming that their awareness is derived solely through divine revelation. It underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the timing of the Hour, a key eschatological theme in Shia theology regarding the signs of resurrection. This distinction reinforces the concept of *tawhid* in attributes, separating the Creator's infinite knowledge from the created beings' limited, bestowed knowledge.
